title: Predicted vs actual
text: Each dot is one game the model never saw. Dots on the dashed line were predicted exactly. Here the typical miss is 9.7 points and R² is 0.51. Games stay spread out around the line because football scoring is noisy.

title: Misses vs prediction
text: A healthy cloud is flat and even around zero. A curve means the model is missing a pattern. A funnel that widens on the right means high-scoring games are harder to call, so the same range would not fit every game.

title: How the misses are shaped
text: The orange bell curve is what perfectly normal misses would look like. Close agreement is why the 80% and 95% ranges can be trusted. Average miss is +0.7 points, so the model is not leaning high or low.

title: Q-Q plot of the misses
text: Dots on the line mean the misses follow a bell curve. Dots peeling away at either end mean more extreme blowouts or shootouts than the bell curve expects.

title: What each input is worth
text: Each dot is how many points the predicted total moves when that input rises by one typical amount (one standard deviation). The bar is the 95% range of that estimate. A bar touching zero means the input might be doing nothing.

title: Which inputs the model leans on
text: Shuffle one input so it carries no information and see how much worse the predictions get. Long bars are inputs the model cannot do without. Tiny bars mean the model barely uses them.

title: Games that bend the fit
text: Each dot is a training game. Height is how much the line would move if that one game were removed. Shown: the 250 most influential games plus a sample of the rest. Dots above the dashed line (5% of all games) deserve a look. No lone dot towering over the rest means no single game is steering the model.

title: Error by season
text: For each season the model was trained only on earlier seasons, then tested on that one. Short blue bars next to gray ones mean it beat the Vegas total line that year. Bars of similar height from year to year mean it holds up over time.

title: Can you trust the ranges?
text: If the 80% range says it covers 80% of games, the dot sits on the dashed line. Dots below the line mean the ranges are too narrow. Dots above mean they are wider than they need to be.

title: What happens as one input changes
text: Blue is the average prediction as one input slides across its range with everything else left alone. Gray lines are individual games. In a linear model they are all parallel straight lines. Curved or fanned lines would be the sign that a different model type could help.

title: Would more data help?
text: Orange is the error on the games the model trained on. Blue is the error on games it had not seen. Lines that have flattened and sit close together mean more seasons would barely help. A big gap between them would mean the model is memorizing.
